title: Steel sub-floor bearers in four prefabricated SIP houses built under national multiple-use approvals
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE Chief Executive determination; Building Act 2004; comparative only, not Alberta)
code_edition: NZ Building Code, First Schedule, Building Regulations 1992 (cited); B2.3.1(a) durability period; edition not stated

facts.text: Four houses built from a prefabricated kit with an assembly manual; floors, walls and roofs are 150 mm structurally insulated panels (SIPs) of coated metal bonded to an EPS core, with 15-degree gable roofs.
The building consents were for work described in national multiple-use approvals issued under section 30F of the Act, and the authority refused code compliance certificates for the as-built work.
Figure 1 shows a kit house (p.4); Figure 2 shows the typical sub-floor construction for all four buildings (p.5); Figure 3 shows the sub-floor construction in more detail (p.6).
The matter is whether galvanised steel sub-floor bearers meet the 50-year durability period in B2.3.1(a).
